subject.title: fix(cli): warn that attach --print-config prints a live bearer token

question: Should `attach --print-config` continue printing the live bearer token by default with this stderr warning, or must the command move to a safer secret-revealing policy?
rationale: The warning is a bounded improvement, but choosing whether a documented setup command may continue emitting live credentials is a product and security-boundary decision rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Accept Warning-Only Behavior
options.body: Preserve the existing stdout handoff contract, merge the warning after real terminal proof, and track any redacted summary mode separately.

options.title: Require Explicit Secret Opt-In
options.body: Change the command so default output is non-secret and require an explicit flag or protected-file handoff to reveal the live token.

options.title: Pause Credential Output Changes
options.body: Leave the current behavior unchanged until maintainers define the complete attach secret-output contract and upgrade expectations.

recommendation.title: Accept Warning-Only Behavior
recommendation.body: Preserve the existing stdout handoff contract, merge the warning after real terminal proof, and track any redacted summary mode separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion explicitly routed this policy choice to this reviewer, while the implementation history owners can advise on the attach workflow contract.
